$comment: THE READ RECORD of slice s-14 of the 1985 rules (kb/Work PB5597; DESIGN-spec-conformance-review.md section 10.6): the reader's and the refuter's files and the flags the slice asked, verbatim, with the digest of each source. Written by audit_batch.py import-reads; read only through lineage_reads.load, the one normalization.

scope-1985: Relative I-O I-O-CONTROL paragraph: RERUN clause (rerun points) accepted
SAME [RECORD] AREA: memory area shared by relative files
RERUN obsolete element: no obligation beyond acceptance

citations.quote: the points at which rerun is to be established
citations.check: OK  §1985:VIII.2.6.1 p1  (2.6.1 Function)  the text is in p1

cases.reason: 1985: 'specifies the points at which rerun is to be established and the memory area which is to be shared by different files'. 2023 dropped RERUN (FMT-12.4.6.2 keeps only APPLY COMMIT and SAME), so no 2023 rule states the rerun half. The probe declares RERUN and SAME RECORD AREA on two relative files, and a MOVE into one file's record shows in the other's.
cases.needs: an own golden from the probe, then its own verdict CONFORMS

citations.quote: pertaining to a relative file
citations.check: OK  §1985:VIII.3.2.1 p1  (3.2.1 Function)  the text is in p1

cases.reason: 1985: 'furnishes information concerning the physical structure, identification, and record-names pertaining to a relative file'. SR-13.4.5.3-7 says only that format 2 is the FD of a relative or indexed file, so it does not state the whole 1985 scope. The other pointers were proposed on wording only.
cases.needs: an own golden from the probe, then its own verdict CONFORMS
